text: Okay, so let's talk a little bit about how pricing is changing for the AI economy because the models we're used to aren't quite working anymore.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We're used to thinking about the value of software as a tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You might spend 10K on Zendesk and then go hire some customer support representatives to actually handle the customer support tickets that are coming into you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But AI is fundamentally shifting how we think about that value.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As products gain agentic capabilities, we're actually able to see them deliver on value, and we can think about their value as an output of that result.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: For example, Intercom's FIN actually goes and manages and resolves customer support requests for you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So as we start thinking about this new model, that value actually starts to become measurable, counted in things like resolutions, commits, workflows completed.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we're forced and incentivized to start thinking about how we price our products to actually communicate that value.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And thinking about this repricing isn't new.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We've done this every time we've had a major technology shift.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We started with the on-prem software, where things were pretty stable after an install, and so a one-time license made sense.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But then we moved to cloud, and your software was getting updated continuously, and so a subscription model started to fit the bill.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And about now is where you expect for me to tell you what the right model for AI is.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I've got some good news and some bad news.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The bad news is we're in the early innings.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We're still figuring this out.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: But the good news is we are seeing some patterns emerge amongst our Stripe data.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Take Rapolit, for example, a developer platform that has been around for almost a decade.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: When agentic coding really started to take off, they pivoted their product and rethought their pricing and have since seen hockey stick growth.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: They started with a flat subscriptions model and then added on credits as AI became core to their product.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Subscriptions for predictability for their users and then usage for value capture.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so the result is that Replit is aiming for a 1 billion ARR this year.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And they're not alone in thinking about their pricing in this way.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Usage-based billing is becoming critical for anybody selling AI services.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: In fact, two in three of the Forbes AI50 companies have some form of usage-based pricing, and many are delivering that sort of hybrid model that Replit is.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The subscription piece helps you anchor in your relationship with your customer and provide them that predictability, and the usage-based billing piece helps scale with the usage that your customer experiences as they grow.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So knowing you need to be usage-based is one thing, but what does that mean in practice?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Here's a few principles to think about.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: First, price in your customer's language.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Developers think in tokens, enterprises think in seats, but more and more everyone is being exposed to and becoming comfortable with consumption.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And so think about how you can communicate the value that your users are receiving in the way that you communicate the price.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Next, you want to give your customers real-time spend visibility before they get their bill.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: No one has opened up their electric bill and thought, huh, that's cheaper than I expected.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You don't want the same to be true with users of your products.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So make sure that you're communicating their real-time usage so that they understand what the cost is going to be at the end of the day.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: This is not just a nice-to-have.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: It's critical to prevent user churn.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Lastly, think about selling credits, not costs.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Have your users exchange money for credits on your product upfront at one time so that when they're using your product, they're thinking about the value that they're experiencing and not the dollars and cents for every action that they're taking.
